name: Rosendin Holdings, Inc. (Rosendin Electric, Inc.)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Rosendin is close to pure-play exposure to the AI data-center electrical build-out — revenue roughly doubled in two years ($2.80B in 2023 to a company-reported $5.6B in 2025), it is now the second-largest US electrical contractor per EC&M's 2025 ranking, and its CEO states customers provide work forecasts 10–20 years out. BACKGROUND: Rosendin Holdings is the parent of Rosendin Electric (electrical contracting) and Modular Power Solutions (off-site electrical manufacturing), founded 1919 in San Jose and 100% employee-owned (ESOP) since 2000 — the largest employee-owned electrical contractor in the US, a claim uncontested in reviewed rankings. 12,000+ employees (2025, company-reported). Core markets: hyperscale data centers (35+ years in the sector, 15+ GW deployed, $7.5B total data-center work value per company), utility-scale solar and BESS EPC through the Rosendin Energy Group, transportation infrastructure, and commercial construction.
ecosystemRole: We assess Rosendin as the ecosystem's build-side: one of the few contractors combining hyperscale data-center electrical delivery with GW-scale renewables and ~10 GWh of installed BESS EPC in-house — the company that physically installs what the app's suppliers sell and the hyperscalers buy. Basis: company disclosures corroborated by EC&M rankings and owner press (Arevon, Recurrent Energy projects). Its BESSUPS partnership with FlexGen (utility-scale BESS replacing data-center UPS and diesel gensets) places it directly in the BESS-for-AIDC product conversation, not just installation.

productsAndServices.name: Data-Center Electrical Construction
productsAndServices.description: Turnkey electrical construction for hyperscale, colocation, AI, and modular data centers — 35+ years in the sector, originating in Silicon Valley. Company-reported scale: 15+ GW of power deployed across data-center projects, $7.5B total data-center work value, 4M+ electrician man-hours of annual capacity, with integrated design-build (~20% of projects) and BIM/IPD delivery.
highlights: Project Goliath (CyrusOne, Sterling VA): 20 MW of electrical infrastructure — 20 diesel generators, 40 UPS, 120 distribution devices — constructed in 26 weeks, a company-claimed construction speed record
MAZ Mesa (AZ) hyperscale campus: design-build electrical with 1,500+ daily workers at peak under GC DPR Construction; client confidential
EC&M's 2025 ranking places Rosendin #2 among US electrical contractors ($3.69B 2024 revenue, +31.8%), behind only utility-T&D-weighted Quanta Services
Customers provide work forecasts 10–20 years out, per CEO Keith Douglas (January 2026) — unusual backlog visibility for construction
productsAndServices.positioning: Company claims to be the leading electrical contractor for hyperscale construction; trade coverage places it top-tier alongside Cupertino Electric (~half its size) among data-center electrical specialists. No independent market-share figure exists. Hyperscaler client names are almost never disclosed — project codenames and confidential-client listings are the norm.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct contracts with hyperscalers, colocation developers, and general contractors; integrated project delivery and design-build
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscale/AI campuses, colocation, enterprise data centers, US-wide
productsAndServices.roadmap: Mountain West regional HQ opened Chandler, AZ (May 2026) for Southwest data-center/semiconductor growth; Richmond, VA logistics + training center near the Virginia data-center corridor (2026)

productsAndServices.name: Prefabrication & Modular Power Solutions (MPS)
productsAndServices.description: In-house prefabrication (conduit, panel assemblies, electric rooms, rooftop assemblies) plus sister company MPS (Sherman/McKinney/Lewisville TX, Mt. Juliet TN), which manufactures skid-built prefabricated electrical rooms and integrated critical-power solutions for data centers, medium/high-voltage, renewables, and BESS markets across North America. Company-reported: 2M+ sq ft of manufacturing space, 7,000+ MW of annual fabrication capacity.
highlights: Prefab positioned as the structural answer to the electrician shortage — converting site labor constraints into factory throughput
Robotic solar installer trial with ULC Technologies (April 2025): 350–400 modules per 8-hour shift with a 2-person crew, roughly triple manual rates, per company
MPS carries its own SVP on the holdings executive team — organizationally first-class, not a support shop
productsAndServices.positioning: Trade coverage describes MPS as a go-to for factory-built data-center electrical; prefab depth at this scale is rare among electrical contractors
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Integrated with Rosendin projects plus direct MPS sales across US, Canada, Mexico

productsAndServices.name: Rosendin Energy Group — Solar & BESS EPC
productsAndServices.description: Turnkey utility-scale EPC: solar (rooftop to 720+ MW single-axis tracker sites), BESS (peak shaving, frequency regulation, grid stability, microgrid support), substations (1–800+ MVA), transmission, and SCADA. Company-reported record over 15 years: ~32 GW of clean energy delivered, 7.1+ GW solar installed, 9.5–10+ GWh of BESS installed, 151 substations, 330+ projects across the US, Canada, Puerto Rico, and Guam.
highlights: Townsite Solar+Storage (Boulder City, NV): 232 MWdc solar + 90 MWac Tesla Megapack BESS — completion corroborated by owner Arevon
Tranquility BESS 72 MW/288 MWh (Recurrent Energy), Garland BESS 88 MW/352 MWh, Mustang BESS 75 MW/300 MWh — named California projects
February 2026: new Energy Group leadership (Billy Watts, ex-Primoris/Mortenson/Siemens Energy) with BESS and substation expansion explicitly aimed at data-center support and grid stability
Exploring floating solar, small modular reactors, and gas turbines per the February 2026 announcement — a whole-of-grid posture beyond renewables
productsAndServices.positioning: Solar Power World ranks Rosendin roughly #8–#10 among national solar contractors/EPCs (2024–2025, company-cited). The differentiator is the combination: few firms hold hyperscale electrical delivery and GW-scale BESS/solar EPC under one roof
productsAndServices.soldThrough: EPC and design-build contracts with project owners and developers (Arevon, Recurrent Energy among corroborated customers)
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale developers, IPPs, utilities, and increasingly data-center-adjacent grid work

productsAndServices.name: BESSUPS & Next-Generation Data-Center Power
productsAndServices.description: Announced June 2025 with FlexGen: a utility-scale BESS engineered to replace traditional data-center UPS systems and diesel generators, sited outside the building at medium voltage — combining Rosendin's patented BESSUPS design with FlexGen's grid-interconnection and transient-frequency-stabilization patents, meeting CBEMA power-quality standards. Separately, an August 2025 partnership with Phinergy brings aluminum-air backup generators (MW-scale, multi-day duration claims) to the US data-center market as a diesel alternative.
highlights: Direct BESS-for-AI-data-center product play — the contractor moving up from installing storage to co-developing it
Phinergy selection came via the Net Zero Innovation Hub (Google, Microsoft, Data4, Vertiv, Schneider) from 70+ proposals
Rosendin SVP Bill Mazzetti: 'Our clients simply need more power, and without it, development stops'
productsAndServices.positioning: Cross-links two ecosystem players: FlexGen (software-first BESS integrator) supplies the controls IP; Rosendin supplies the delivery machine and data-center customer base
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Joint commercialization with FlexGen; early stage
productsAndServices.targetSegments: AI data-center operators seeking UPS/diesel alternatives and faster power
productsAndServices.roadmap: Commercialization announced June 2025; no deployed-site count published yet

productsAndServices.name: Transportation & Commercial Sectors
productsAndServices.description: Aviation (security, networks, radio systems), transit (traction power, catenary, train control — BART, Caltrain, WMATA, LAX among named), highway ITS, plus commercial, healthcare, semiconductor, biotech, education, and entertainment construction (Crypto.com Arena, SoFi Stadium, Oracle Park among historical projects). 24/7 service and maintenance operations.
highlights: Diversification base that predates and cushions the data-center concentration
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Public agency and commercial construction contracts
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Transit agencies, airports, commercial owners across 11 sectors

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Rosendin as near-pure-play exposure to the AI data-center electrical build-out: revenue roughly doubled in two years ($2.80B in 2023 → $3.69B in 2024 → ~$5.6B in 2025), moving it to #2 among US electrical contractors. Basis: EC&M rankings corroborate the company's figures, and the growth timing matches the hyperscaler capex cycle exactly.

(Moderate confidence) We assess prefabrication is the scaling strategy: 7,000+ MW of annual fabrication capacity and MPS's factory-built electrical rooms convert the industry's binding constraint — skilled electricians — into factory throughput; the robotic solar trial extends the same logic to field labor.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the Energy Group is being deliberately converged with the data-center franchise: BESSUPS with FlexGen (BESS replacing UPS/diesel), the Phinergy backup partnership, and stated SMR/gas-turbine exploration read as a play to sell data-center customers power capacity, not just electrical installation — because, per its own SVP, without power 'development stops.'

(Moderate confidence) We assess the ESOP structure functions as a talent-retention moat in a labor-short market and permits patient investment; the cost is disclosure — financials are company-reported and unaudited publicly. Collection gap: no independent verification exists for the 9.5–10 GWh BESS aggregate or backlog claims, though owner press corroborates individual projects.
